2.2.3.2 Fauna
Page 2-32
Paragraph three, the Clemson salamander, and the other races of Plethodon Jordani, are no longer recognized as subspecies. Their status has been reduced to that of different color phases. These color phases do not occur In local areas as originally thought, rather, they are each widely scattered throughout the range of P. jordani. Thus, the Clemson phase is not restricted to the Bad Creek area. (See Conant, R. 1975. A field guide to reptiles and amphibians of eastern and central North America. 2nd edition. Houghton Mifflin Co. Boston. Also see other data previously supplied in Enclosure #21 of supplemental information of 8 Oct. 1974).
Section 2.2.3.2 has been revised.
